items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: And it’s the same with Joe Farnsworth and John Webber, and those are the first people I call... We can play a whole concert without even discussing one bit of music.

ctx.x: That’s great. Do you have, I know it’s sort of hard this day and age to have a working band, you know, keep this group together and I’m going to give them enough work to stick with me.

Yeah. Or I guess you can put them on retainer. I mean I can’t do that. You know I have my number one guys, my pool of guys that I always want to work with. And I try to get them first. And then if I have to go outside that pool I have another pool that is the second tier or whatever. But it’s pretty obvious from my recordings and you see me on gigs, who are the guys I want. If I have a choice I’m calling Harold [Mabern] right away all the time. He can’t make everything, so then there are people I move on from…
What do you say to a student, one of those people who is in a constant search, if I only had this horn, if I only had this mouthpiece, if I only could find a good reed?
